answer: One robust defense is staking bonded reputation: every agent must lock a refundable deposit of quartz-graded collateral before it can wander freely across marketplaces, and each identity carries a verifiable thread of past transactions signed by its key. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, while honest agents keep their stake and build a longer thread of trust. Misbehavior slashes the deposit, so the cost of a sybil attack scales linearly with the number of fake identities, making large-scale fakery economically irrational.
